# Wasserstein contraction of the augmented kernel {#sec-wasserstein-lifting}

The preceding construction identifies a stationary law without requiring a metric contraction of the augmented process. We now impose assumptions that give a quantitative bound on its transition kernel. The argument applies to a contractive memory update more generally than the affine EMA recursion.

## Metrics and a coupled driving chain

Let $(\mathsf X,d_X)$ be Polish and let $(\mathsf Y,d_Y)$ be a complete separable memory space. On $\mathsf Z=\mathsf X\times\mathsf Y$ use

$$
d_Z((x,u),(y,v))=d_X(x,y)+d_Y(u,v).
$$ {#eq-product-metric}

Write $\mathcal P_1(\mathsf Z)$ for probabilities with finite first moment in $d_Z$. For $\mu,\eta\in\mathcal P_1(\mathsf Z)$, the $1$-Wasserstein distance satisfies the primal and Kantorovich--Rubinstein dual representations,

$$
\begin{aligned}
W_{d_Z}(\mu,\eta)
&=\inf_{\gamma\in\mathcal C(\mu,\eta)}
\int d_Z(z,z')\,\gamma(dz\,dz')\\
&=\sup_{\|f\|_{\operatorname{Lip}(d_Z)}\leq1}
|\mu(f)-\eta(f)|.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-wasserstein-duality}

For a Markov kernel $K$ write

$$
\tau_{d_Z}(K)=\sup_{z\ne z'}
\frac{W_{d_Z}(K(z,\cdot),K(z',\cdot))}{d_Z(z,z')}.
$$ {#eq-dobrushin-coefficient}

Fix a parameter region $\mathsf K\subseteq\Theta$. The constants below may depend on $\mathsf K$, but not on $\theta\in\mathsf K$.

::: {#asm-driver-coupling}
## Geometrically contracting driver coupling

For every $\theta\in\mathsf K$ there is a Markovian coupling of two $P_\theta$-chains, with joint law denoted by $\mathbb P^\theta_{x,y}$, such that for every $n\geq0$ and $x,y\in\mathsf X$,

$$
\mathbb E^\theta_{x,y}d_X(X_n,\widetilde X_n)
\leq C_P\rho_P^n d_X(x,y),
\qquad C_P<\infty,\quad 0<\rho_P<1.
$$ {#eq-driver-trajectory-coupling}
:::

This is an estimate for one coupled pair of *trajectories*, at every time. A bound on $W_{d_X}(P_\theta^n(x,\cdot),P_\theta^n(y,\cdot))$ for each $n$, considered separately, does not by itself specify a consistent coupling of the intervening observations.

::: {#asm-memory-lipschitz}
## Contractive and spatially regular memory update

For $\theta\in\mathsf K$, the update $T_\theta:\mathsf X\times\mathsf Y\to\mathsf Y$ is measurable and, with constants $r<1$ and $L_T<\infty$ independent of $\theta$,

$$
d_Y(T_\theta(x,u),T_\theta(y,v))
\leq r\,d_Y(u,v)+L_Td_X(x,y).
$$ {#eq-memory-joint-lipschitz}

For one, hence every, fixed $z_0\in\mathsf Z$, assume $Q_\theta(z_0,\cdot)\in\mathcal P_1(\mathsf Z)$.
:::

The last assumption is a one-step moment condition. It can be verified from a driver drift inequality and the growth of the memory forcing.

::: {#thm-wasserstein-lifting}
## Wasserstein contraction lifts through contractive memory

Suppose @asm-driver-coupling and @asm-memory-lipschitz hold. For every $\eta\in(\max\{\rho_P,r\},1)$ there is $C_Z(\eta)<\infty$, uniform in $\theta\in\mathsf K$, such that

$$
W_{d_Z}(Q_\theta^n(z,\cdot),Q_\theta^n(z',\cdot))
\leq C_Z(\eta)\eta^n d_Z(z,z'),
\qquad n\geq0.
$$ {#eq-augmented-contraction}

In particular $\tau_{d_Z}(Q_\theta^n)\leq C_Z(\eta)\eta^n$. Each $Q_\theta$ has a unique invariant distribution $\nu_\theta$ in $\mathcal P_1(\mathsf Z)$, and

$$
W_{d_Z}(\delta_zQ_\theta^n,\nu_\theta)
\leq C_Z(\eta)\eta^n W_{d_Z}(\delta_z,\nu_\theta).
$$ {#eq-invariant-wasserstein-rate}
:::

::: {.proof}
Fix $\theta$. Couple two driving paths according to @asm-driver-coupling, and evolve the corresponding memories using those paths. Put $e_n=\mathbb E^\theta_{x,y}d_Y(U_n,\widetilde U_n)$. By @eq-memory-joint-lipschitz and induction,

$$
e_n\leq r^n d_Y(u,v)
+L_T\sum_{j=1}^n r^{n-j}
\mathbb E^\theta_{x,y}d_X(X_j,\widetilde X_j).
$$

Together with @eq-driver-trajectory-coupling this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E^\theta_{x,y}d_Z(Z_n,\widetilde Z_n)
\leq {}& C_P\rho_P^n d_X(x,y)+r^n d_Y(u,v)\\
&+L_TC_P\sum_{j=1}^n r^{n-j}\rho_P^j d_X(x,y).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-memory-geometric-convolution}

For $\eta>\max\{r,\rho_P\}$, the geometric convolution is bounded by $c_\eta\eta^n$ with $c_\eta<\infty$. The law of the coupled augmented paths is a coupling of the two $n$-step transition laws. Taking it as a candidate in the primal Wasserstein formula proves @eq-augmented-contraction.

At $n=1$ this gives $\tau_{d_Z}(Q_\theta)<\infty$. In conjunction with $Q_\theta(z_0,\cdot)\in\mathcal P_1$, the triangle inequality shows that $Q_\theta$ maps $\mathcal P_1(\mathsf Z)$ into itself. Choose $m$ such that $C_Z(\eta)\eta^m<1$. Then $\mu\mapsto\mu Q_\theta^m$ is a strict contraction on the complete space $(\mathcal P_1(\mathsf Z),W_{d_Z})$, so Banach's fixed-point theorem supplies a unique fixed point $\nu_\theta$. Since $\nu_\theta Q_\theta$ is also fixed by $Q_\theta^m$, uniqueness gives $\nu_\theta Q_\theta=\nu_\theta$. Finally, apply @eq-augmented-contraction to the coupling of $\delta_z$ and $\nu_\theta$.
:::

When @asm-frozen-driver holds with the corresponding finite moments, @cor-stationary-memory-law identifies this invariant distribution with the law of the stationary infinite-history memories. Thus the Wasserstein construction gives a quantitative route to the same frozen expectation, without requiring a backward iteration in its proof. Uniqueness among all invariant probabilities also follows from @prp-fuh-stationarity under its hypotheses; @thm-wasserstein-lifting itself asserts uniqueness in $\mathcal P_1$.

## Affine EMA updates and Lyapunov moments

For @eq-memory-map, use $d_Y(u,v)=\|u-v\|$ and write

$$
T_\theta(x,u)=Au+b_\theta(x),\quad
A=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha I_d,\beta I_d),\quad
b_\theta(x)=\begin{pmatrix}(1-\alpha)H_\theta(x)\\(1-\beta)H_\theta(x)^{\odot2}\end{pmatrix}.
$$ {#eq-affine-memory}

If $b_\theta$ is $L_b$-Lipschitz in $d_X$, then @asm-memory-lipschitz holds with $r=\max\{\alpha,\beta\}$ and $L_T=L_b$. In particular, a bound on the second moment of $H_\theta$ is not alone a spatial Lipschitz estimate for $b_\theta$ in an arbitrary metric. The metric and the innovation regularity must be checked together.

A drift inequality gives a complementary first-moment bound. Suppose for a measurable $w:\mathsf X\to[1,\infty)$,

$$
P_\theta w\leq aw+B,\qquad
\|T_\theta(x,u)\|\leq r\|u\|+c_0+c_1w(x),
\qquad a,r<1.
$$ {#eq-driver-memory-drift}

Choose $\delta\in(\max\{a,r\},1)$ and $k>0$ sufficiently large that $(k+c_1)a\leq\delta k$. With

$$
\mathcal V(x,u)=1+kw(x)+\|u\|,
$$ {#eq-augmented-lyapunov}

the augmented transition satisfies

$$
Q_\theta\mathcal V\leq\delta\mathcal V+L,\qquad L<\infty.
$$ {#eq-augmented-drift}

Indeed, $Q_\theta\mathcal V(x,u)\leq1+(k+c_1)P_\theta w(x)+r\|u\|+c_0$, and substitution of @eq-driver-memory-drift gives the claim. If $w(x)$ is comparable to $1+d_X(x,x_0)$, this drift is naturally aligned with the first moment in $d_Z$. For an invariant law with finite $\mathcal V$-moment, invariance yields $\nu_\theta(\mathcal V)\leq L/(1-\delta)$. In the metric of @eq-product-metric, the corresponding first eccentricity is

$$
\int d_Z(z_0,z)\,\nu_\theta(dz)<\infty,
$$

as required for the $p=1$ Wasserstein Poisson theory of [@Hofstadler2026].

## The normalised Adam observable

There is a distinction between regularity of the memory update and regularity of its readout. The map $(m,v)\mapsto m/(\sqrt v+\varepsilon)$ is not globally Lipschitz in $v$ under the ordinary Euclidean metric near $v=0$. For a bounded innovation, however, a change of memory coordinates removes this difficulty without modifying the Adam recursion.

Assume, for the remainder of this subsection, that

$$
\|H_\theta(x)\|_\infty\leq B_H,\qquad
\|H_\theta(x)-H_\theta(y)\|\leq L_Hd_X(x,y).
$$ {#eq-bounded-innovation}

Put $S_n=\sqrt{V_n}$ coordinatewise and use the forward-invariant memory set

$$
\mathsf Y_B=\{(m,s):\|m\|_\infty\leq B_H,\quad
0\leq s_i\leq B_H\},
$$

with metric $d_Y((m,s),(m',s'))=\|m-m'\|+\|s-s'\|$. With initial memories $(M_0,S_0)\in\mathsf Y_B$, the update is

$$
\widehat T_\theta(x,m,s)=
\begin{pmatrix}
\alpha m+(1-\alpha)H_\theta(x)\\
\sqrt{\beta s^{\odot2}+(1-\beta)H_\theta(x)^{\odot2}}
\end{pmatrix}.
$$ {#eq-sqrt-memory-update}

For each coordinate, the second component is the Euclidean norm of $(\sqrt\beta\,s_i,\sqrt{1-\beta}\,H_{\theta,i}(x))$. The reverse triangle inequality therefore gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
d_Y(\widehat T_\theta(x,u),\widehat T_\theta(y,v))
\leq {}&\max\{\alpha,\sqrt\beta\}\,d_Y(u,v)\\
&+\bigl(1-\alpha+\sqrt{1-\beta}\bigr)L_Hd_X(x,y).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-sqrt-memory-contraction}

Thus the transformed memory still satisfies @asm-memory-lipschitz, with contraction coefficient $\max\{\alpha,\sqrt\beta\}<1$. On $\mathsf Y_B$ the Adam readout

$$
G(m,s)=\frac{m}{s+\varepsilon}
$$ {#eq-adam-lipschitz-readout}

is Lipschitz:

$$
\|G(m,s)-G(m',s')\|
\leq\varepsilon^{-1}\|m-m'\|
+B_H\varepsilon^{-2}\|s-s'\|.
$$ {#eq-adam-readout-lipschitz}

This is an alternative metric representation of the same finite-dimensional memory process, not a change in its update rule. It gives a direct Lipschitz observable for the Poisson equation when the innovation is bounded, as for an acceptance-rate residual. For unbounded innovations the affine $(m,v)$ representation still admits @thm-wasserstein-lifting under its stated assumptions; the Lipschitz property of the Adam readout must then be addressed separately.
